checkpoints.description: [1/5] Plan: verified all 14 report findings as TRUE and fix the top-priority adoption gaps - F1 add an optional game bind_input hook the engine calls after building InputMap, F2 move asset rebinding into core so AssetRegistry consumers rebind scene nodes, F13 single-source the version and add --version plus CHANGELOG

impact_assessment.why: Every actionable claim in reports/keystone-improvement-2026-11-08.md was verified against live source by execution: engine constructs InputMap() with no game hook at app.py:59, DEFAULT_BINDINGS lacks fire/reload/slot/jump, AssetRegistry.refresh never touches a scene while rebinding lives only in web/editor.py:965, apply_pose has no mask, Scene has one point_light slot, instancing keys on id(), plan draw_calls is a node count, widgets expose only panel/button, no VersionedStore, and ARCHITECTURE.md claims v0.46.0 while the package is 0.45.0 with no CHANGELOG or --version.
impact_assessment.benefits: A game can finally deliver its own live controls; hot reload rebinds any AssetRegistry consumer instead of only the web editor; version drift and missing changelog stop misleading cold-starting agents.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive GameModule hook and a new reload_assets helper plus CLI flag; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: no persisted format change - existing scenes and bindings still load.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep every change additive and optional, keep default paths byte-identical, pin each fix with a failing-first test, and verify the canonical simulate hash plus all 6 project gates.

[1/6] Plan: verified all remaining report findings F3,F4,F5,F6,F8,F9,F10,F11,F12,F14 TRUE by execution; fix the six additive ones - F3 apply_pose channel mask, F4 camera up()/basis(), F6 honest batch metrics plus content-keyed grouping, F8 Canvas text measuring and a clamped label row, F9 deterministic texture patterns, F12 scene budget/fingerprint test helpers; defer F5 light list, F10 sprite nodes, F11 versioned store and F14 History removal as they need shader/schema work or break the public API

impact_assessment.why: Every remaining claim reproduced: apply_pose zeroed a simulated position, the camera has no up/basis, two content-identical meshes produce 2 instancing groups, plan_batches hides instanced_calls while plan_instanced exposes it, Canvas cannot measure text although keystone.ui.font.text_width exists, TextureData has only checker/from_png, keystone.testing has no budget helper, and History has no production consumer.
impact_assessment.benefits: Animation can layer on simulation-owned nodes, viewmodel code stops re-deriving the camera basis, render metrics mean one thing each, HUD labels can be measured and clamped instead of clipping, procedural textures stop being hand-rolled per game, and testbeds can assert budgets instead of brittle exact counts.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive parameters and helpers only; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: no persisted format change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep every default path byte-identical, prove each fix failing-first, verify pixels and the canonical simulate hash are unchanged, and run the full 6/6 gate.

[1/3] Plan: verified F7 (the one untriaged report finding) true in all four parts by execution; implement the report's stated first slice - read-only on_frame/on_event observers plus an events frame map on run_bot, and load_policy with a --policy module:factory CLI form

impact_assessment.why: run_bot had no per-frame hook, no evidence module existed, --policy accepted only three built-ins, and agents.observe is a snapshot adapter, so the consumer ships its own 739-line play harness and 107-line bot and core playtest stays unvalidated against real content.
impact_assessment.benefits: A game collects its own telemetry and registers its own bot policy without forking the runner.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive run_bot keywords and a broadened --policy value; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: no transcript or persisted format change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep observers read-only, pin that the transcript and hash are identical with and without them, and run the full 6/6 gate plus the canonical simulate hash.

[1/3] Plan: adversarial defect hunt on the public API - found and fixed a quadratic/O(n^4) texture preset cost with an unbounded allocation, and a lock bypass where set_node and set_selection_properties mutated locked nodes

impact_assessment.why: TextureData.pattern ran per-pixel Python loops (panel 180ms, rivets 288ms at 512x512, rivets O(size^4)) with no size bound, and a locked editor node could still be renamed, re-layered, re-tagged, hidden or bulk-edited because two handlers omitted the guard their siblings call.
impact_assessment.benefits: Procedural textures are linear in pixel count with a 16 MB ceiling; an editor lock now blocks every mutation path rather than most of them.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: lock now rejects two more actions; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: no persisted format change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Prove pixel-identical output for the perf rewrite against a reference implementation, extend the lock regression to enumerate the new paths, and verify no suite test relied on the permissive behaviour.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Both fixes implemented and verified - texture presets proven pixel-identical across 9 sizes (including odd ones) with panel 180ms->2ms and rivets 288ms->6.5ms at 512x512 plus a 2048 size ceiling; lock matrix shows all 13 mutating actions now blocked; play matrix shows all 15 blocked; probes confirmed PNG round-trips, corrupt-PNG rejection, atomic writes, non-finite JSON rejection and undo/redo/batch/prefab-edit integrity all correct

[3/3] Project gate 6/6 on both commits; 986 tests 0 failures; canonical --simulate hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and reference PNG 4899B unchanged; pushed 1c34cd4 and 6b27f81; checklists: passed

[1/3] Plan: fixed the WAV encode/decode asymmetry found by an adversarial IO probe - read_wav scaled negatives by 32768 and positives by 32767 while write_wav scaled both by 32767, so every negative sample drifted one step toward zero on round trip and -1.0 decoded as -0.99997

impact_assessment.why: The error is asymmetric distortion, not quantization, and the existing round-trip test compared one positive sample at places=2 so it could not detect it.
impact_assessment.benefits: WAV round-trips are symmetric and full-scale values are exact; audio evidence and hashes are trustworthy.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: decoded sample values change by up to one step; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: no file format change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Divide both signs by 32767 and clamp for the external -32768 case, prove the odd-symmetry invariant with a regression, and run the full 6/6 gate.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Fixed and verified - read_wav divides both signs by 32767 and clamps to [-1,1]; negatives and positives now carry identical error magnitude and +/-1.0 round-trips exactly; regression asserts the odd-symmetry invariant plus a one-step bound; 1000 tests pass; canonical hash unchanged; 6/6 gate; pushed 4509abd

[3/3] Additional probes found no defects: physics/character (floor rest, jump, wall stop, determinism), triggers (enter/stay/exit/teleport), broadphase vs brute force over 60 queries, raycast nearest+filter, glTF import and rejection, material graph evaluation and cycle/dangling rejection, scene and prefab library round-trips with trash restore, headless and UI render determinism, and Engine cleanup on build_scene/bind_input failure; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-wav-symmetry-v1' completed successfully.
